entries.title: Differential Diagnosis of Acute Abdominal Pain (Surgical Approach)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2 is titled 'Acute abdominal pain' and this study unit is Toronto Notes' surgical differential-diagnosis approach to the identical presentation.

testable_competencies.acute_abd_pain_ddx: Generate and prioritize a surgical differential diagnosis for acute abdominal pain by location/quadrant, and identify features suggesting a surgical emergency (peritonitis, hemodynamic instability).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2 ('Abdominal masses and pelvic masses') is the presentation this study unit's differential-diagnosis approach directly addresses.

testable_competencies.abd_mass_ddx: Generate a surgical differential diagnosis for an abdominal mass by location and characteristics, and identify features requiring urgent surgical referral.

entries.title: Differential Diagnosis of Gastrointestinal Bleeding (Surgical Approach)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1 ('Upper gastrointestinal bleeding') is one half of the GI-bleeding differential this study unit covers.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2 ('Lower gastrointestinal bleeding') is the other half of the GI-bleeding differential this study unit covers.

testable_competencies.gi_bleed_ddx: Localize GI bleeding as upper vs. lower, generate a surgical differential, and recognize indications for urgent surgical/endoscopic intervention.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 49 is titled 'Jaundice' and this study unit is the chapter's surgical (obstructive-cause-focused) approach to the identical presentation.

testable_competencies.jaundice_ddx_surgical: Differentiate surgical (obstructive) from non-surgical causes of jaundice and identify indications for biliary decompression or surgical referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74-3 ('Pre-operative medical evaluation') explicitly covers identification of perioperative cardiopulmonary, anesthetic, and thromboembolic risk and strategies to minimize perioperative morbidity/mortality - the same content as this study unit.

testable_competencies.preop_assessment: Perform a preoperative risk assessment (cardiopulmonary, thromboembolic, medication-related) and identify strategies to minimize perioperative morbidity/mortality.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1 ('Fever and hyperthermia') provides the general fever-evaluation framework this postoperative-specific study unit applies (infectious and inflammatory postsurgical causes).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74-3's perioperative-risk framework includes recognizing and managing postoperative complications, of which fever is a common early sign.

testable_competencies.postop_fever_ddx: Apply a systematic timeline-based differential (wind, water, walking, wound, wonder drugs) to postoperative fever and identify when further investigation/intervention is required.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74-3's perioperative-risk-identification scope encompasses recognition of postoperative surgical-site complications such as infection and dehiscence.

testable_competencies.wound_complications: Recognize surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, and incisional hernia as postoperative wound complications and identify appropriate management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-1 ('Acute kidney injury') covers prerenal/renal/postrenal AKI causes relevant to the postoperative AKI content of this study unit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 111-1 ('Lower urinary tract symptoms') covers urinary retention, the classic postoperative urinary complication addressed here.

testable_competencies.postop_urinary_renal: Recognize and initiate management of postoperative urinary retention and acute kidney injury.

entries.title: Postoperative Respiratory Complications (Dyspnea, Atelectasis, Pneumonia, Pulmonary Embolism)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 27 ('Dyspnea') is the presentation this postoperative-dyspnea/respiratory-complications study unit directly addresses.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 7's causal-conditions list names pulmonary embolism as a hemoptysis-associated cardiac/vascular cause, relevant to postoperative respiratory decompensation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14's causal-conditions list names pulmonary embolus/infarction and pneumothorax among pulmonary chest-pain causes overlapping postoperative respiratory complications.

testable_competencies.postop_resp_complications: Recognize and initiate management of postoperative dyspnea, atelectasis, pneumonia, and pulmonary embolism, and identify patients requiring urgent escalation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74-3 explicitly lists myocardial ischemia, heart failure, and arrhythmia as perioperative cardiopulmonary risks to identify and manage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14 ('Chest pain') covers postoperative myocardial ischemia presenting as chest pain.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 13 ('Cardiac arrest') is relevant only to the most severe postoperative cardiac decompensation, not the full spectrum this study unit covers.

testable_competencies.postop_cardiac: Recognize postoperative myocardial ischemia, arrhythmia, and heart failure and initiate appropriate management/escalation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's causal-conditions list names hepatic abscess and splenic abscess among localized-pain causes, the same abscess/localized-infection mechanism as this postoperative complication.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1's infectious-fever framework applies to intra-abdominal abscess as a postoperative infectious source of fever.

testable_competencies.postop_abscess: Recognize intra-abdominal abscess as a cause of persistent postoperative fever/pain and identify indications for drainage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Adynamic (paralytic) ileus' as a bowel-dilatation cause of abdominal distension.

testable_competencies.paralytic_ileus: Differentiate paralytic ileus from mechanical bowel obstruction and initiate appropriate supportive management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 58-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Postsurgical' as a delirium cause, directly matching this study unit.

testable_competencies.postop_delirium: Recognize postoperative delirium, identify and treat reversible contributing causes, and apply nonpharmacologic prevention strategies.

entries.title: Approach to the Solitary Pulmonary Nodule

testable_competencies.spn_approach: Recognize risk factors distinguishing benign from malignant solitary pulmonary nodules and identify when further imaging/biopsy is indicated.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective evidence found for this specific incidental-finding workup topic; framing/background for Lung Cancer only.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 7's causal-conditions list names 'Neoplasms (e.g., bronchogenic carcinoma)' as an airway-disease cause of hemoptysis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 54-1's middle-mediastinum category names 'Tumours (e.g., bronchogenic cancer)', relevant only to centrally-located lung cancer presenting as a mediastinal mass.

testable_competencies.lung_cancer_recognition: Recognize presenting features of lung cancer (hemoptysis, weight loss, mass) and identify appropriate initial investigation and referral pathway.

entries.title: Pleura, Lung, and Mediastinum (Overview)
entries.zero_question_reason: Organizational overview heading; content is covered by its constituent disease-specific study units.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 76's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'parapneumonic, empyema' together as one infectious/inflammatory exudative-effusion category.

testable_competencies.empyema_management: Recognize complicated parapneumonic effusion and empyema, and identify indications for pleural drainage/tube thoracostomy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Pneumothorax' as a pulmonary/mediastinal chest-pain cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 13's causal-conditions list names 'tension pneumothorax' as a noncardiac cause of cardiac arrest, relevant to the emergency-recognition depth of this study unit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pneumothorax is a recognized dyspnea-causing pulmonary process under objective 27's scope.

testable_competencies.pneumothorax_recognition: Recognize simple, traumatic, and tension pneumothorax; distinguish tension pneumothorax as an immediate life threat requiring emergency needle decompression.

entries.title: Tube Thoracostomy (Chest Tube Insertion)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 76's management of pleural effusion/empyema commonly requires tube thoracostomy, the intervention this study unit covers.

testable_competencies.chest_tube_indications: Identify indications for tube thoracostomy (pneumothorax, hemothorax, empyema, complicated effusion) and recognize major complications.

do_not_test: Step-by-step chest tube insertion technique - procedural/specialist detail.

entries.title: Lung Transplantation
entries.zero_question_reason: Transplant candidacy criteria and surgical technique are specialist-level content beyond generalist MCCQE scope.

entries.title: COPD (Surgical and Perioperative Considerations)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 27's causal-conditions list names COPD as an airway cause of dyspnea.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 74-3 explicitly names 'chronic obstructive pulmonary disease' among pulmonary perioperative-risk factors to identify.

testable_competencies.copd_perioperative: Recognize COPD as a major perioperative pulmonary risk factor and as a candidacy consideration for lung-volume-reduction/transplant referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Primary ownership of COPD diagnosis/medical management is expected to belong to Respirology (R). This GS study unit is scoped to perioperative risk and surgical-candidacy considerations only; final PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK decision deferred to the post-32-chapter global overlap pass.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 54-1 is titled 'Mediastinal mass' and directly matches this study unit's anterior/middle/posterior compartment approach.

testable_competencies.mediastinal_mass_ddx: Localize a mediastinal mass by compartment (anterior, middle, posterior) and generate an appropriate differential diagnosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 54-1's anterior-mediastinum category explicitly names 'thymoma' as a tumour cause.

testable_competencies.thymoma_recognition: Recognize thymoma as the classic anterior mediastinal mass and its association with myasthenia gravis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 54-1's posterior-mediastinum category explicitly names 'esophageal cancer' as a tumour cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 118-2's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'esophageal cancer' as a medical-disease cause of weight loss.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 26's esophageal-dysphagia mechanical-obstruction category covers the progressive dysphagia that is esophageal carcinoma's classic presentation.

testable_competencies.esophageal_ca_recognition: Recognize progressive dysphagia and weight loss as red-flag features of esophageal carcinoma and identify appropriate initial investigation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14's gastrointestinal chest-pain category (esophageal spasm/esophagitis) provides the closest causal-conditions evidence for esophageal-source acute chest pain; esophageal perforation itself is not separately named.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's upper-abdominal region causal-conditions list does not explicitly name esophageal perforation; retained as the nearest acute-abdominal/thoracic-pain evidence for this surgical emergency.

testable_competencies.esophageal_perforation_recognition: Recognize esophageal perforation (e.g., post-endoscopic instrumentation or Boerhaave syndrome) as a surgical emergency and initiate urgent management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 54-1's posterior-mediastinum category explicitly names 'hiatal hernia' as an 'other' cause of a posterior mediastinal mass/opacity.

testable_competencies.hiatus_hernia_recognition: Recognize sliding vs. paraesophageal hiatus hernia and identify indications for surgical repair (e.g., paraesophageal hernia with volvulus risk).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 26's esophageal-dysphagia category explicitly names 'lower esophageal sphincter' dysfunction among intermittent mechanical/motor causes, the classic achalasia presentation.

testable_competencies.achalasia_recognition: Recognize achalasia's classic presentation (dysphagia to solids and liquids) and identify appropriate diagnostic workup (manometry, barium swallow).

entries.title: Peptic Ulcer Disease (Surgical Complications)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1's causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Peptic ulcer disease' as an ulcerative/erosive upper-GI-bleeding cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's upper-abdominal-region causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Peptic ulcer disease, gastritis'.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 14's gastrointestinal chest-pain category explicitly names 'Peptic ulcer disease'.

testable_competencies.pud_surgical_complications: Recognize perforated and bleeding peptic ulcer as surgical emergencies and identify indications for operative vs. endoscopic/medical management.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Peptic ulcer disease etiology and medical management are primarily mapped in Gastroenterology (G, SU-G-14). This GS unit is scoped to surgical complications and operative indications.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2's gastrointestinal-neoplasm category covers gastric malignancy as a cause of abdominal mass.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-3's upper-abdominal-region causal-conditions list names 'Malignancy' as a chronic-abdominal-pain cause.

testable_competencies.gastric_ca_recognition: Recognize alarm features suggesting gastric carcinoma and identify appropriate initial investigation (endoscopy with biopsy).

entries.title: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumour (GIST)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2's gastrointestinal-neoplasm category explicitly names 'gastrointestinal stromal tumour' as an example abdominal-mass cause.

testable_competencies.gist_recognition: Recognize gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) as a mesenchymal (non-epithelial) GI neoplasm distinct from adenocarcinoma.

entries.zero_question_reason: Low coverage weight/uncommon diagnosis; recognition-only depth with no dedicated minimum question coverage.

entries.title: Bariatric Surgery

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 118-1 ('Obesity') covers assessment and care-plan collaboration for obesity, of which bariatric surgery is a recognized management option; the objective does not itself detail surgical technique or operative selection.

testable_competencies.bariatric_indications: Recognize general indications for bariatric surgery and major postoperative complications (e.g., anastomotic leak, nutritional deficiency, dumping syndrome).

do_not_test: Specific bariatric operative technique/procedure selection - specialist detail.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's bowel-dilatation category explicitly names 'Mechanical obstruction (e.g., adhesions, volvulus)' as a cause of abdominal distension.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's lower-abdominal-region causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Bowel obstruction' and 'Incarcerated hernia' as causes.

testable_competencies.sbo_management: Recognize mechanical small bowel obstruction, distinguish partial from complete and simple from strangulated obstruction, and identify indications for surgical vs. nonoperative management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's diffuse-pain causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Ischemic bowel disease'.

testable_competencies.intestinal_ischemia_recognition: Recognize acute mesenteric ischemia as a surgical emergency with pain out of proportion to exam findings and initiate urgent management.

entries.title: Tumours of the Small Intestine

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2's gastrointestinal-neoplasm category covers small bowel tumours as an abdominal-mass cause.

testable_competencies.small_bowel_tumour_recognition: Recognize small bowel tumours as an uncommon but important cause of obscure GI bleeding, obstruction, or intussusception.

entries.zero_question_reason: Uncommon diagnosis with recognition-only depth; no dedicated minimum question coverage.

entries.title: Large Intestine (Anatomy and Overview)
entries.zero_question_reason: Background anatomy/overview; not independently testable but frames the disease-specific units that follow.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's vascular category explicitly names 'diverticulosis' as a lower-GI-bleeding cause.

testable_competencies.diverticulosis_recognition: Recognize diverticulosis as the most common cause of acute lower GI bleeding and distinguish it from diverticulitis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's lower-abdominal-region causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Diverticulitis'.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-3's lower-abdominal-region causal-conditions list explicitly names 'Diverticular disease'.

testable_competencies.diverticulitis_management: Diagnose acute diverticulitis, grade severity, and initiate appropriate management including identifying indications for urgent surgical intervention (e.g., perforation, abscess, obstruction).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's neoplastic category explicitly names 'polyp' as a lower-GI-bleeding cause.

testable_competencies.colorectal_polyps: Recognize adenomatous polyps as premalignant lesions and identify appropriate screening/surveillance/removal principles.

entries.title: Familial Colorectal Cancer Syndromes

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's neoplastic causal-conditions category is the only GI-bleeding-adjacent evidence identified; it does not name hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes specifically.

testable_competencies.hereditary_crc_recognition: Recognize red-flag features (young age, family history pattern) suggesting a hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome (e.g., Lynch syndrome, FAP) and identify indications for genetics referral.

entries.zero_question_reason: Rare hereditary syndromes with weak direct MCC evidence; recognition-only depth, primary detail deferred to Medical Genetics (MG).
entries.cross_discipline_note: Genetic counseling and syndrome-specific surveillance detail overlap with Medical Genetics (MG). This GS unit is scoped to surgical recognition/referral only.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's neoplastic category explicitly names 'carcinoma' as a lower-GI-bleeding cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2's gastrointestinal-neoplasm category explicitly names 'colon tumour' as an abdominal-mass cause.

testable_competencies.crc_management: Recognize presenting features of colorectal carcinoma, stage-appropriate initial workup, and general surgical management principles.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's vascular category explicitly names 'angiodysplasia' as a lower-GI-bleeding cause.

testable_competencies.angiodysplasia_recognition: Recognize angiodysplasia as a vascular cause of lower GI bleeding, particularly in older adults.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's bowel-dilatation category explicitly names 'volvulus' as an example of mechanical obstruction causing abdominal distension.

testable_competencies.volvulus_recognition: Recognize sigmoid and cecal volvulus, interpret the classic imaging findings, and identify indications for urgent decompression/surgery.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1's adynamic-ileus category explicitly names 'toxic megacolon' as an example cause of abdominal distension.

testable_competencies.toxic_megacolon_recognition: Recognize toxic megacolon as a life-threatening complication of colitis (infectious or inflammatory) and initiate emergency management.

entries.title: Fistula (Enteric/Colonic)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-4's anorectal-disease category names 'fistulas' as an anorectal-pain cause; enterocolonic fistula (e.g., enterocutaneous, colovesical) is the broader surgical entity this study unit addresses.

testable_competencies.gi_fistula_recognition: Recognize enterocutaneous, colovesical, and other GI fistulas as complications of Crohn's disease, diverticulitis, or surgery.

entries.zero_question_reason: Moderate-evidence complication topic; recognition-only depth with no dedicated minimum question coverage.

entries.title: Stomas (Colostomy/Ileostomy)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective specifically addresses stoma creation/complications; objective 2's abdominal-mass framework is the nearest adjacent evidence for stoma-related complications (e.g., parastomal hernia presenting as a mass).

testable_competencies.stoma_basics: Recognize indications for temporary vs. permanent colostomy/ileostomy and common stoma complications (e.g., prolapse, parastomal hernia, high-output stoma).

entries.zero_question_reason: No dedicated MCC objective evidence; WEAK mapping strength, recognition-only depth.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-4's anorectal-disease category explicitly names 'Hemorrhoids' as an anorectal-pain cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-2's anorectal-disease category explicitly names 'hemorrhoids' as a lower-GI-bleeding cause.

testable_competencies.hemorrhoid_management: Distinguish internal from external hemorrhoids, grade internal hemorrhoids, and identify indications for medical vs. procedural/surgical management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-4's anorectal-disease category explicitly names 'Fissures' as an anorectal-pain cause.

testable_competencies.anal_fissure_management: Diagnose anal fissure from history/exam and initiate first-line medical management before considering surgical sphincterotomy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-4's anorectal-disease category is the closest presentation match for anorectal abscess as a cause of anorectal pain, though the objective's causal list does not name abscess explicitly.

testable_competencies.anorectal_abscess_management: Recognize anorectal abscess and initiate urgent incision and drainage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-4's anorectal-disease category explicitly names 'fistulas' as an anorectal-pain cause.

testable_competencies.fistula_in_ano: Recognize fistula-in-ano as a common sequela of anorectal abscess and identify general management principles.

entries.title: Pilonidal Disease

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-4 names 'Coccygeal pain' as an anorectal-pain category, the closest available evidence for pilonidal disease though it is not named explicitly.

testable_competencies.pilonidal_disease_recognition: Recognize pilonidal disease presenting as a sacrococcygeal abscess or chronic draining sinus.

entries.zero_question_reason: WEAK indirect mapping strength; recognition-only depth with no dedicated minimum question coverage.

entries.title: Rectal Prolapse
